data.title: Re-read pages through the codec when rekeying instead of trusting the cache
data.body:
Changes proposed in this pull request:

sqlite3_rekey_v2 rewrites every page by fetching it with sqlite3PagerGet, which returns a page already in the pager cache without passing it through the codec again. If a page was read before rekey is called and its ciphertext is then changed on disk, rekey never reads or authenticates those bytes. It re-encrypts the cached copy under the new key and returns SQLITE_OK. The database then opens under the new key and passes cipher_integrity_check, and the old key no longer opens it, so the tampering is never reported.

This change clears the pager cache at the start of rekey, right after the existing check that refuses rekey inside a transaction. Every page in the loop is then read from disk and checked by the codec under the current key, so a tampered page makes rekey fail and roll back. The clear sits before the data version is captured, so it does not trip the check that aborts when another connection changed the database.

The new test caches a table, flips one byte of a page on disk, and checks that rekey fails, the new key cannot open the file, and the old key still can.

On beta without the change, rekey reports ok and only the new key works.

The same problem exists on prerelease too (in an extended form which is partially fixed in beta), but I opened it directly on beta as I imagine this is were your efforts are focused now.

data.title: Intermittent "database disk image is malformed" after `ROLLBACK TO` undoes a `DROP TRIGGER` (4.12.0 – 4.19.0)
data.body:
### Expected Behavior

After `SAVEPOINT s; DROP TRIGGER t; ROLLBACK TO s; RELEASE s;` on an encrypted database, the
schema is restored and the connection keeps working. This is what happens with the same
sequence on an unencrypted database, and with a full `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` on an encrypted one.

### Actual Behavior

Roughly once in every 1000 runs, a statement executed after the `ROLLBACK TO` fails with
`database disk image is malformed` (SQLITE_CORRUPT, 11). The failing statement is either the
next `DROP TRIGGER` inside a new savepoint or a plain `SELECT … FROM sqlite_schema`. It never
fails before the first `ROLLBACK TO` has run.

The database file is **not** damaged. After closing the connection and reopening the file with
the same key, `PRAGMA integrity_check` returns `ok` and all triggers are present. This held for
every failure we observed. It looks like stale in-memory state (page cache or schema) after
the partial rollback.

The failure depends on the encrypted content. Each page is encrypted with a random IV, so the
same script fails or passes from run to run, and we could not make it deterministic. Results
with the script below (shell built from the release tags, Linux x86_64, OpenSSL 3.5.5):

| SQLCipher (SQLite) | Variant | Iterations | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.19.0 (3.53.4) | `SAVEPOINT; DROP TRIGGER; SELECT sqlite_schema; ROLLBACK TO; RELEASE` | 20000 | 21 |
| 4.19.0 (3.53.4) | same without the `SELECT` | 20000 | 7 |
| 4.19.0 (3.53.4) | `BEGIN; DROP TRIGGER; SELECT; ROLLBACK` (control) | 10000 | 0 |
| 4.19.0 (3.53.4) | savepoint sequence **without a key** (control) | 20000 | 0 |
| 4.13.0 (3.51.2) | savepoint sequence | 10000 | 7 |
| 4.12.0 (3.51.1) | savepoint sequence | 10000 | 6 |

We first saw it through the Python binding `sqlcipher3-wheels` 0.5.7, which bundles 4.12.0
with OpenSSL 3.6.0. It shows the same rate on Linux and on Windows 11. With that binding, a
`ROLLBACK TO` that only undoes data changes (`UPDATE`, `PRAGMA user_version`) did not fail in
5000 runs: the schema change seems to be required.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Build the shell from a release tag, as in the README:
   ```
   git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.19.0 https://github.com/sqlcipher/sqlcipher.git && cd sqlcipher
   ./configure --with-tempstore=yes CFLAGS="-DSQLITE_HAS_CODEC -DSQLITE_EXTRA_INIT=sqlcipher_extra_init -DSQLITE_EXTRA_SHUTDOWN=sqlcipher_extra_shutdown" LDFLAGS="-lcrypto"
   make sqlite3
   ```
2. Run `bash repro.sh ./sqlite3 20000 savepoint`. The script is below, released under CC0,
   so feel free to use it in your tests.
3. Each iteration:
   - creates a fresh database with a random raw key (`PRAGMA key = "x'…'"`);
   - creates 10 tables and 13 triggers in one transaction;
   - runs `SAVEPOINT s; DROP TRIGGER dN; SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'trigger'; ROLLBACK TO s; RELEASE s;` for 4 triggers;
   - reads `sqlite_schema` once more.

   Failures print the error and the result of reopening the file:

   ```
   [303] Parse error near line 31: database disk image is malformed (11) | reopened: integrity_check, trigger count = ok 13
   ```

<details><summary>repro.sh (CC0)</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Intermittent "database disk image is malformed" after ROLLBACK TO undoes a DROP TRIGGER
# on an encrypted database. Uses only the SQLCipher command-line shell and bash.
#
# Usage: repro.sh <path to the sqlcipher shell> [iterations] [variant]
#   variant: savepoint (default) | no_read | transaction (control) |
#            plaintext (control: the savepoint sequence with no key, i.e. not encrypted)
#
# Each iteration creates a fresh database with a random 256-bit raw key, creates 10 tables
# and 13 triggers in one transaction, then drops and restores 4 triggers. The shell runs
# with -bail, so the first error stops it and is printed. On failure the database is
# reopened with the same key and checked with PRAGMA integrity_check.
#
# License: CC0 1.0 Universal (public domain dedication),
# https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ - use it freely, e.g. in your tests.
set -euo pipefail

SQL_SHELL="${1:?path to the sqlcipher shell}"
N="${2:-10000}"
VARIANT="${3:-savepoint}"
WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${WORKDIR:?}"' EXIT

READ="SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'trigger';"

schema() {
  echo "BEGIN;"
  for i in $(seq 0 9); do
    echo "CREATE TABLE t$i (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, a TEXT NOT NULL, b BLOB, c INTEGER);"
  done
  local events=(UPDATE DELETE INSERT INSERT)
  for n in 0 1 2 3; do
    echo "CREATE TRIGGER d$n BEFORE ${events[$n]} ON t0 WHEN $n >= 0 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'trigger $n'); END;"
  done
  for i in $(seq 1 9); do
    echo "CREATE TRIGGER e$i BEFORE UPDATE OF a ON t$i BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'table $i'); END;"
  done
  echo "COMMIT;"
}

script() {
  [ "$VARIANT" = plaintext ] || echo "PRAGMA key = \"x'$1'\";"
  schema
  for n in 0 1 2 3; do
    case "$VARIANT" in
      transaction) echo "BEGIN; DROP TRIGGER d$n; $READ ROLLBACK;" ;;
      no_read) echo "SAVEPOINT s; DROP TRIGGER d$n; ROLLBACK TO s; RELEASE s;" ;;
      *) echo "SAVEPOINT s; DROP TRIGGER d$n; $READ ROLLBACK TO s; RELEASE s;" ;;
    esac
  done
  echo "$READ"
}

"$SQL_SHELL" :memory: <<< "PRAGMA key = \"x'00'\"; SELECT 'sqlite ' || sqlite_version(); PRAGMA cipher_version; PRAGMA cipher_provider_version;" | tail -n +2 | tr '\n' ' '
echo "| $(uname -sr)"

failures=0
for i in $(seq 1 "$N"); do
  db="${WORKDIR:?}/test-$i.db"
  key="$(od -An -tx1 -N32 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
  if ! err="$(script "$key" | "$SQL_SHELL" -bail "$db" 2>&1 >/dev/null)"; then
    failures=$((failures + 1))
    if [ "$VARIANT" = plaintext ]; then
      reopened="$(printf 'PRAGMA integrity_check;\n%s\n' "$READ" | "$SQL_SHELL" "$db" 2>&1 | tr '\n' ' ')"
    else
      reopened="$(printf 'PRAGMA key = "x%s";\nPRAGMA integrity_check;\n%s\n' "'$key'" "$READ" \
        | "$SQL_SHELL" "$db" 2>&1 | tail -n +2 | tr '\n' ' ')"
    fi
    echo "[$i] ${err//$'\n'/ } | reopened: integrity_check, trigger count = $reopened"
  fi
  rm -f "${db:?}"
done
echo "$VARIANT: $N iterations, $failures failures"
```

</details>

SQLCipher version: 4.19.0 community (also 4.12.0 and 4.13.0); SQLite 3.53.4; OpenSSL 3.5.5;
Linux x86_64 (WSL2, kernel 6.18). Default settings apart from the raw key.

data.title: `cipher_integrity_check` reports HMAC failures on pages a VFS preallocated
data.body:
### Expected Behavior

`PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check` returns no rows for an intact database, whatever chunk size or preallocation the VFS applies.

### Actual Behavior

With `SQLITE_FCNTL_CHUNK_SIZE` set, the unix VFS rounds the file up to the chunk, and `cipher_integrity_check` reports every zero block past the end of the database as `HMAC verification failed`. The loop in `sqlcipher_codec_ctx_integrity_check` runs up to `sqlite3OsFileSize`, so it checks blocks that were never database pages. The browser `opfs-sahpool` VFS does the same on every `SQLITE_FCNTL_SIZE_HINT`.

### Steps to Reproduce

On Linux with `gcc`, `make`, `tcl` and the OpenSSL headers installed:

```sh
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/sqlcipher/sqlcipher && cd sqlcipher
./configure --with-tempstore=yes CFLAGS="-DSQLITE_HAS_CODEC -DSQLITE_EXTRA_INIT=sqlcipher_extra_init -DSQLITE_EXTRA_SHUTDOWN=sqlcipher_extra_shutdown" LDFLAGS="-lcrypto"
make sqlite3
rm -f ic.db
printf "PRAGMA key='test';\n.filectrl chunk_size 65536\nCREATE TABLE t(a); INSERT INTO t VALUES(1);\n" | ./sqlite3 ic.db
wc -c < ic.db
./sqlite3 ic.db "PRAGMA key='test';" "PRAGMA page_count;" "PRAGMA integrity_check;" "PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check;" "PRAGMA cipher_version;"
```

Output:

```text
ok
65536
ok
2
ok
HMAC verification failed for page 3
HMAC verification failed for page 4
HMAC verification failed for page 5
HMAC verification failed for page 6
HMAC verification failed for page 7
HMAC verification failed for page 8
HMAC verification failed for page 9
HMAC verification failed for page 10
HMAC verification failed for page 11
HMAC verification failed for page 12
HMAC verification failed for page 13
HMAC verification failed for page 14
HMAC verification failed for page 15
HMAC verification failed for page 16
4.20.0 community
```

The file is 65536 bytes, the database has 2 pages and `PRAGMA integrity_check` passes, yet pages 3 to 16 fail. The same loop is on `beta`.

SQLCipher version: 4.20.0 community (`master` 355d4db9, SQLite 3.54.1)

data.title: Generate a random salt when a page is encrypted before the salt is known
data.body:
A new database reads its salt from the first 16 bytes of the file and falls back to random bytes only when that read fails. The read happens when page 1 is first encrypted, after `pager_write_pagelist` has sent `SQLITE_FCNTL_SIZE_HINT`. A VFS that grows the file on that hint, like the unix VFS with `SQLITE_FCNTL_CHUNK_SIZE` or the browser `opfs-sahpool` VFS, makes the read return zeros, so every new database gets the same all-zero salt.

This generates the salt when a page is encrypted before the salt is known. A connection decrypts page 1 of an existing database before writing to it, so this only happens for a new file. Existing databases still read the salt from the header. `beta` has the same code.

data.title: Refuse PRAGMA cipher_migrate on a read-only main database
data.body:
A connection opened read-only through the URI parameters `mode=ro` or `immutable=1` runs `PRAGMA cipher_migrate` to success and rewrites the database file. `db->openFlags` is recorded before the URI is parsed and never carries `mode=ro`, so the `ATTACH` of the `-migrated` file, the export and the rename onto the main file all go through. With `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY` the migration fails only because that `ATTACH` cannot create the `-migrated` file, which returns `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` and leaves the connection in the deferred error state.

The main btree is read-only on all three routes, so the check reads it once the legacy format has been detected and before any file is created. It returns `SQLITE_READONLY` and exits through `cleanup` like the other checks that run before the database is touched, which leaves the file unchanged and the connection usable. A read-only connection on a database already in the current format still gets 0, since nothing needs to be written. For `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY` the result changes from 14 to 8 on purpose, so every read-only route reports the same cause.

data.title: Keep URI parameters when cipher_migrate reopens the main database
Guard `BtShared.nRef` reads with `SQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE`
data.body:
SQLCipher 5.0.0-beta.1 no longer compiles with `SQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE`. The shared-cache fix in 1825a0af reads `BtShared.nRef` in the `cipher_migrate` refusal and in an `assert` in `sqlcipher_ctx_set_error`, and SQLite declares `nRef` only when shared cache is compiled in. Builds that omit shared cache, such as the `sqlite-wasm-rs` Wasm build, stop with `'BtShared' has no member named 'nRef'`.

Both reads now sit under `#ifndef SQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE`, the same guard SQLite puts around the field. Without shared cache `Btree.sharable` is never set, so `ctx->shared` stays 0 and neither check could fire. Builds with shared cache compile exactly the code they did before.

The shared-cache tests in the core, compatibility and rekey suites are skipped with `ifcapable shared_cache` when shared cache is omitted, since a `cache=shared` URI then opens a private cache and those tests cannot hold. That lets the SQLCipher suite run on a build without shared cache.

data.title: One corrupt encrypted page poisons subsequent integrity_check reads on the same connection
data.body:
## Version and environment

Reproduced from SQLCipher commit `810db22f575ee7cf94ea96a3e91622b5fcece3dc` on Linux amd64, using SQLite 3.53.3 / SQLCipher 4.17.0 Community and the bundled SQLCipher 4 `testkey` database.

## Describe the bug

After exactly one encrypted page fails HMAC verification, SQLCipher stores a persistent codec/pager error. `PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check` correctly identifies page 17 as the only modified page, but a subsequent standard `PRAGMA integrity_check` on the same connection reports many earlier pages and page 1 as unreadable. Those extra reports are caused by the poisoned state, not additional on-disk corruption.

## Minimal reproduction

```sh
timeout 900 sqlcipher-022-single-corrupt-encrypted-page-poisons-current-integrit-f3ef876c/poc/reproduce_corrupt_page_integrity_poison.sh
```

The essential data mutation and query sequence is:

```sh
cp sqlcipher-4.0-testkey.db corrupt.db
dd if=/dev/zero of=corrupt.db bs=4096 count=1 seek=16 conv=notrunc
sqlcipher corrupt.db <<'SQL'
.bail off
PRAGMA key='testkey';
PRAGMA cipher_integrity_check;
PRAGMA integrity_check;
SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_schema;
SQL
```

Run the same SQL on an unmodified copy as the control.

## Actual behavior/output

The clean control returns `ok`, `ok`, and `1`. The corrupt copy first returns:

```text
HMAC verification failed for page 17
Tree 2 page 17: btreeInitPage() returns error code 11
```

It then reports pages 16 through 3 and page 1 as `unable to get the page. error code=1`. Stderr contains `sqlcipher_codec_ctx_set_error 1`, `identified deferred error condition: 1`, and finally `file is not a database`.

## Expected behavior

The integrity diagnostics should identify the actual failed page without turning its page-local authentication error into unrelated later read failures. Subsequent pages should be independently checked when safe, or the check should stop with an explicit global-abort result rather than misreporting a wider corruption set.

## Impact and scope

The cascade exaggerates corruption scope and can mislead repair, restore, monitoring, and forensic decisions. This candidate concerns diagnostic accuracy on the current connection, not acceptance of corrupted data.

## Relevant source/root cause

`sqlite3Codec()` calls `sqlcipher_codec_ctx_set_error()` on decrypt failure around `src/sqlcipher.c:3459-3470`. Later reads detect this stored error around `:3414-3423`, set pager error, and return a zeroed buffer. `sqlite3pager_error()` around `src/pager.c:8057-8060` moves the pager into `PAGER_ERROR`, while `cipher_integrity_check` itself can identify the page mismatch around `src/sqlcipher.c:2096-2103`.

## Suggested regression test

Modify exactly one page in a multi-page encrypted fixture. Run `cipher_integrity_check` followed by `integrity_check` on the same connection and assert either a page-17-only diagnostic or a clear aborted-check status, never fabricated failures for untouched pages.

## Reproduction bundle

Attached: `sqlcipher-022-single-corrupt-encrypted-page-poisons-current-integrit-f3ef876c_attachment.zip`. It contains the focused PoC, validation evidence, and candidate metadata.

[sqlcipher-022-single-corrupt-encrypted-page-poisons-current-integrit-f3ef876c_attachment.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31178851/sqlcipher-022-single-corrupt-encrypted-page-poisons-current-integrit-f3ef876c_attachment.zip)

data.title: Project is insufficiently renamable from "sqlite" to "sqlcipher"
data.body:
Hello, there are many references to "sqlite" in the software,

https://github.com/sqlcipher/sqlcipher/blob/810db22f575ee7cf94ea96a3e91622b5fcece3dc/sqlite.pc.in#L11

I understand that sqlcipher is a near-ABI-compatible soft fork of sqlite, leading to many internal instances of sqlite that might be difficult for you to automatically rename, but unfortunately, the instances of sqlite are polluting outwards into distributions of the software and conflicting with the file names of the upstream files in the sqlite packages in the same distributions.

This has led to the need for many distributions to modify the files of the sqlcipher software post-installation in a convoluted way, including but not limited to:

- [Debian](https://salsa.debian.org/debian/sqlcipher/-/blob/18e80ddaf2657f60baa2d1779dc17c7bba4d6b43/debian/rules#L51)
- [Arch Linux](https://gitlab.archlinux.org/archlinux/packaging/packages/sqlcipher/-/blob/194a63832ea7559c15f4613ce3cf26a6368779c2/PKGBUILD#L73)
- [OpenSUSE](https://build.opensuse.org/projects/server:database/packages/sqlcipher/files/sqlcipher.spec?expand=1&rev=98f79590f87402c009bf8738c7618a57)
- [LigurOS](https://gitlab.com/liguros/liguros-repo/-/blob/b107c2aa5cd035f4a289a6b51e0c31e641ba6caa/dev-db/sqlcipher/sqlcipher-4.16.0.ebuild?blame=1#L71)
- [Termux](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/blob/7a2dd9fc60c52437807484961f380b70ab48275e/packages/sqlcipher/build.sh#L71)
- [OpenMamba](https://src.openmamba.org/rpms/sqlcipher/src/commit/a1b89140a9357cd88fa86e1353ecf9d1d788c85f/sqlcipher.spec#L106)
- [OpenBSD](https://github.com/openbsd/ports/blob/347157506a6fe18f1ef63277d81c163f84badb16/databases/sqlcipher/Makefile#L50)
- [FreeBSD](https://cgit.freebsd.org/ports/tree/databases/sqlcipher/Makefile?id=e9f01757b5b01424c3c70e1648cd234588b907d4#n38)



and unfortunately, I am struggling with this problem and the need to manually script renaming the files to avoid conflicts is frustrating to handle in my distribution's build framework.

There is an option `libsqlite3.DLL.basename` that can be set to `sqlcipher`, to rename some of the files successfully,


https://github.com/sqlcipher/sqlcipher/blob/810db22f575ee7cf94ea96a3e91622b5fcece3dc/main.mk#L1114

However, it only renames these specific files:


#### What `libsqlite3.DLL.basename=libsqlcipher` does
|before|after|
|:--- |:--- |
|libsqlite3.so.3.53.3|libsqlcipher.so.3.53.3|
|libsqlite3.so.0|libsqlcipher.so.0|
|libsqlite3.so|libsqlcipher.so|

it does not rename these specific other files that are also installed alongside `libsqlcipher.so` into the distributed package:

- `sqlite3`
- `sqlite3.h`
- `sqlite3ext.h`
- `sqlite3.pc`
- `sqlite3.1.gz`

I believe that providing one or more additional options alongside `libsqlite3.DLL.basename` that could be used to preemptively rename the rest of the conflicting files to `sqlcipher*` instead of `sqlite3*` would be very helpful for all future distributions of sqlcipher and also for future updates to all of the above preexisting distributions, to adopt the new variables and dramatically simplify their build scripts.

data.title: Please bump SONAME when removing library symbols.
data.body:
At the moment the library SONAME version is 0.  To work well in a Linux environment with programs linked to the shared library, the library should change SONAME version every time a non-backwards compatible change is done.  One example like this is the removal of symbols.

While working on updating sqlcipher in Debian, I discovered that several times between the current Debian release 3.4.1 and the latest version 4.5.5 backwards compatibility was broken without changing the SONAME.

To update the SONAME, the -version-info "8:6:8" statement in Makefile.in need to be updated, and the diff between the first and third number need to increase.  At the moment the SONAME version is 8-8=0, while in the new version in Debian I plan to move to 9:6:8 to get 9-8=1.

https://tracker.debian.org/sqlcipher

data.title: Would you accept a provider based on native Win32 APIs?
data.body:
On Windows, for various reasons it can be painful to build and bundle third-party cryptography libraries like OpenSSL, NSS, or LibTomCrypt.

As of Windows 7[^winver], it's completely possible to support SQLcipher's needs by using the functionality in the [Windows CNG APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/seccng/cng-portal) (e.g. `bcrypt.{lib,dll}`), which is shipped and updated with the operating system.

That is, if a provider were written based on this, it would allow SQLcipher users on Windows to avoid having to build/link/distribute a third party cryptography library, since they'd just be using the "native" crypto API on the platform (similar to how macOS/iOS users can use CommonCrypto). I don't mind contributing this (and have started on it [here](https://github.com/thomcc/sqlcipher/tree/bcrypt), although it is still WIP), and maintaining it for you -- it would simplify my own open source code[^oss].

Unfortunately, I noticed that you've stopped accepting new providers. This makes sense, but I'm hoping you might make an exception for one based on native win32 APIs provided by the OS. So, is there any chance you'd accept it?

[^oss]: Concretely: I want this because it will simplify maintenance of [rusqlite](https://github.com/rusqlite/rusqlite), which has a fair amount of complexity from building and statically linking a copy of OpenSSL on Windows, mostly to support a use case where users want SQLcipher and don't want to manage any C dependencies themselves. If SQLcipher had a provider that used native windows APIs, I could migrate these users to that.

[^winver]: These APIs were added in Windows Vista, but SQLcipher would need at least Windows 7 (e.g. for `BCryptDeriveKeyPBKDF2`).

data.title: Swift Package Manager Support
data.body:
### Expected Behavior

Being able to install SQLCipher using a Swift Package Manager package maintained by Zetetic

### Actual Behavior

In order to use SQLCipher with Swift Package Manager, a user must generate an amalgamation themselves and create their own Package.swift, e.g. https://github.com/antwork/SQLCipher or https://github.com/groue/GRDB.swift/pull/556

### Steps to Reproduce

N/A

SQLCipher version: 4.4.0

Hello,

While I wish this was a pull request adding a `Package.swift` to the repo instead of an issue requesting one, SQLCipher's amalgamation step complicates this. As far as I know there is currently no SPM equivalent to the `prepare_command` used in `SQLCipher.podspec.json` to generate the amalgamation. An SPM package can easily be made by including an amalgamation as seen in the links above, but since the amalgamation is quite large, it understandably is not included in the SQLCipher repo.

Would Zetetic be open to maintaining a repo that's an iOS/macOS-compatible amalgamation and `Package.swift`, similar to the one linked above? Since installing dependencies with Swift Package Manager is now directly integrated into Xcode, it will inevitably replace CocoaPods as the de-facto dependency management solution for Xcode projects.

Thank you for this project and taking the time to read this!
